blocks.text: What you need before you start

You need Google Chrome on a Mac running macOS 13 Ventura or later. Google's help center gives that as the minimum for Chrome on Mac. If your Mac is older, the current Chrome will not install, so these steps will not help. To check your version, open the Apple menu and choose About This Mac. The macOS version appears near the top of the window.

Chrome also updates often. Google says a new Chrome update arrives every four weeks. An out of date copy can show a print dialog that differs from the one described here. Before you troubleshoot anything, open Chrome, install any pending update, and restart the browser.

blocks.text: Open the print dialog in Chrome

Click once on the page to make Chrome the active window. Then press ⌘P. Chrome opens the print dialog with a preview of the page on screen. Google's help center lists ⌘P as the print shortcut on Mac. You can also choose File > Print from the menu bar. Both routes open the same dialog, so use whichever you remember.

Wait for the preview before you change anything. The preview shows how the saved file will look, including where the page breaks fall. Long pages take longer to lay out, so give the preview time to finish before you judge the page count.
Choose Save as PDF as the destination

The Destination setting decides where the output goes. Open the Destination dropdown and choose Save as PDF. The same list shows your installed printers and Save to Google Drive. Pick Save as PDF when you want a file on your Mac. Pick a printer when you want paper.

blocks.text: Check Destination before every save. If you last printed to paper, the dialog may still point at that printer. Glance at the dropdown each time, then confirm it reads Save as PDF before you press Return or click Save.
Pick which pages go into the PDF

Pages controls the range of the document. All saves every page the preview shows. Current page keeps only the page you are on, which helps when a site splits an article into several pages. Odd/Even pages keeps alternating pages, which suits two-sided printing. Custom range lets you type the page numbers you want.

For a custom range, type the first and last page you want with the word to between them. Then watch the page count in the preview. A leftover number in the box can make the PDF shorter than you expect. Clear the box and retype it if the count looks wrong.
Set the layout and paper size

Layout offers Portrait and the sideways option. Portrait suits most articles, receipts, and letters. The sideways option suits wide tables, charts, and spreadsheets. Switch between them and read the preview. A table cut off at the right edge usually needs the sideways option or a smaller scale, not a different browser.

Paper size sits under More settings. Choose the paper you plan to print on, if you plan to print at all. If the PDF is only for reading on a screen, the default is usually fine. Keep the file simple, and check it once before you share it.
Margins, scale, headers, and background

Click More settings to reveal the rest of the controls. Margins offers Default, None, Minimum, and Custom. Use Minimum when you want more of the page on each sheet. Use None when you want the content to reach the edges of the paper.

Scale offers Default, Fit to printable area, and Custom %. Fit to printable area shrinks a wide page so it fits inside the margins. That option often fixes cut-off edges. Custom % lets you type your own size. Lower it a little if text still runs past the edge.

Headers and footers is an on or off toggle. Turn it off when you do not want extra text printed at the top and bottom of each page. Background graphics is also a toggle. Turn it on when the page depends on colored boxes, shaded rows, or background images to look right. Check the preview after each change.
Save the file and choose where it goes

When the preview looks right, click Save. A save sheet opens. Choose a folder, enter a file name, and use a name you will recognize later, such as the article title with the year. Click Save again to write the file.

The keyboard works too. Press Return to save with the current settings. Press Escape to close the dialog without saving anything. Escape is the fastest way out when a setting goes wrong, and no file is written.
Check the PDF in Finder

Open Finder and go to the folder you chose. Select the file and press the Space bar to preview it. Look at the first page, a page in the middle, and the last page. Confirm that the text reads clearly and the images look the way they did on the web page.

If something looks wrong, go back to the print dialog and change one setting at a time. Save each attempt under a new name, so you keep the version that worked. Overwriting the only copy makes it hard to compare results.
Mistakes people make when saving a web page as PDF

items: Leaving Destination on a printer. No file appears, and paper comes out instead.
Forgetting that Pages may be set to Current page. You get one page from a long article.
Skipping the preview. The preview is the closest look you get before the file exists.
Turning off Background graphics on a page with shaded tables. The tables lose their color.
Saving over an older PDF with the same name. Add the date to the file name instead.

blocks.text: When to save to Google Drive instead

Save to Google Drive writes the PDF straight into your Drive instead of your Mac. That suits files a team needs to find later. Google's printing help article also covers Drive, including Drive for desktop and the Drive website. If you only need the file on your own Mac, stick with Save as PDF.

If the page you want is a spreadsheet, see [how to export Google Sheets as PDF on Mac](/how-to/export-as-pdf-in-google-sheets). That guide covers the export options built into Sheets, which differ from the print dialog described here.
Problems and fixes for PDFs from Chrome

If Save as PDF is missing, update Chrome first. Google ships a new update every four weeks, so an out of date copy is the first thing to rule out. If the preview is blank, close the dialog with Escape, let the page finish loading, and press ⌘P again.

Missing background colors and images usually come from the Background graphics toggle. Turn it on under More settings and check the preview again. Extra text at the top and bottom of the page comes from Headers and footers, which you can turn off in the same section.
A page that runs past the right edge needs a layout or scale change, not a new save. Try the sideways option under Layout first. If the edge still gets cut, set Scale to Fit to printable area.
Quick reference for the keyboard

Three keys cover most of this process. ⌘P opens the print dialog. Return saves with the current settings. Escape cancels without saving. Learn those three, and the rest of the dialog is a matter of checking the preview.

faq.question: Can I save a web page as a PDF in Chrome without another app?
faq.answer: Yes. Chrome's print dialog has Save as PDF in the Destination list, so a basic save needs no extra software. Press ⌘P, choose Save as PDF, then click Save. The file goes wherever you tell the save sheet to put it.

faq.question: What is the Chrome print shortcut on Mac?
faq.answer: ⌘P opens the print dialog. Google's Chrome Help article lists the same shortcut for Mac. Once the dialog is open, Return saves with the current settings and Escape closes it without saving.

faq.question: Why is Save as PDF missing from the Destination list?
faq.answer: Start by updating Chrome. Google says a new update arrives every four weeks, so an old copy can be behind. Then press ⌘P again and check the Destination list before you save.

faq.question: Which macOS version does Chrome on Mac need?
faq.answer: Google says Chrome on Mac requires macOS 13 Ventura or newer. If your Mac runs an older version, the current Chrome will not run, so these steps will not apply to it.

faq.question: Can I save just one page of a long article?
faq.answer: Often yes. Set Pages to Current page, or choose Custom range and type the pages you want. The preview shows the page count, so check it before you click Save.

faq.question: Can I send the PDF straight to Google Drive?
faq.answer: Yes. Choose Save to Google Drive from the Destination list instead of Save as PDF. Google's printing help article also covers Drive, including Drive for desktop and the Drive website.

faq.question: Why are the background colors missing from my PDF?
faq.answer: Background graphics is an on or off toggle under More settings. If it is off, colors and images in the page background may not appear. Turn it on, check the preview, then save again.

faq.question: Why is my PDF cut off at the right edge?
faq.answer: The page is wider than the printable area. Switch Layout to the sideways option, or set Scale to Fit to printable area under More settings. Then check the preview again before you save.

steps.name: Open the web page in Chrome
steps.text: Open the web page in its own Chrome tab. Wait until the text and images finish loading, so the preview shows the whole page. Then move to the next step.
steps.tip: Scroll to the bottom once. Some pages load more images as you scroll.

steps.name: Open the print dialog
steps.text: Press ⌘P, or choose File > Print from the menu bar. Chrome opens the print dialog with a preview of the page.
steps.tip: Both routes open the same dialog.

steps.name: Set Destination to Save as PDF
steps.text: Open the Destination dropdown near the top of the dialog and choose Save as PDF. The list also shows your installed printers and Save to Google Drive.
steps.tip: If Save as PDF is missing, update Chrome and open the dialog again.

steps.name: Choose which pages to include
steps.text: Open Pages and pick All, Current page, Odd/Even pages, or Custom range. For Custom range, type the first and last page with the word to between them.
steps.tip: Watch the page count in the preview before you save.

steps.name: Pick Portrait or the sideways layout
steps.text: Open Layout and choose Portrait or the sideways option. Use the sideways option for wide tables and spreadsheets. Check the preview for cut-off edges.
steps.tip: The preview updates as soon as you change the layout.

steps.name: Adjust More settings
steps.text: Click More settings. Set Paper size, Margins, and Scale. Turn Headers and footers and Background graphics on or off, then check the preview again.
steps.tip: Fit to printable area often fixes a page that runs past the margins.

steps.name: Click Save and choose a folder
steps.text: When the preview looks right, click Save. In the save sheet, choose a folder and enter a file name. Click Save again to write the file.
steps.tip: Return saves with the current settings. Escape closes the dialog without saving.

steps.name: Check the PDF in Finder
steps.text: Open Finder, go to the folder you chose, and select the file. Press the Space bar to preview it, then check the first page, a middle page, and the last page.
steps.tip: If the file looks wrong, save a new version under a new name.

troubleshooting.problem: Save as PDF is not in the Destination list
troubleshooting.fix: Update Chrome, since Google ships a new update every four weeks, then open the print dialog again with ⌘P.
Close the dialog with Escape, let the page finish loading, then press ⌘P again.

troubleshooting.problem: Background colors or images are missing
troubleshooting.fix: Turn on Background graphics under More settings, then check the preview before you save.

troubleshooting.problem: Text runs past the right edge
troubleshooting.fix: Switch Layout to the sideways option, or set Scale to Fit to printable area under More settings.

troubleshooting.problem: Extra text appears at the top and bottom of each page
troubleshooting.fix: Turn off Headers and footers under More settings, then check the preview again.
